facts.content: 3 days of diarrhea, vomiting, and feeling feverish.
facts.source_text: CC: 3 days diarrhea, vomiting, and feverishness

facts.content: Diarrhea started watery, now very loose, occurring four or more times today, with no blood.
facts.source_text: Diarrhea started watery, now very loose; ≥4x today; no blood

facts.content: Patient has been vomiting everything including water and tea, with the last episode approximately 2 hours ago after breakfast.
facts.source_text: Vomiting everything incl water/tea; last episode ~2 hrs ago after breakfast

facts.content: Patient reports a subjective high temperature but does not have a thermometer.
facts.source_text: Subjective high temp; no thermometer

facts.content: Patient is urinating okay, last urinated about 1 hour ago, urine color unknown.
facts.source_text: Urinating OK; last urinated ~1 hr ago; urine color unknown

facts.content: Periumbilical pain is tender around the navel, intermittent and colicky, with an urge to defecate.
facts.source_text: Periumbilical pain, tender around navel; intermittent/colicky, urge to defecate

facts.content: Patient has no rash and baseline bowel movements once per day.
facts.source_text: No rash; baseline bowels 1x/day

facts.content: Patient has had contact with a brother who has a similar illness and reports a school outbreak, with no recent travel.
facts.source_text: Contact: brother with similar illness; reports school outbreak; no travel

facts.content: Denies prior abdominal issues or surgery and has intermittent dysmenorrhea.
facts.source_text: PMH/PSH: Denies prior abdominal issues/surgery; dysmenorrhea intermittently

facts.content: Takes Vitamin D daily.
facts.source_text: Meds: Vitamin D daily

facts.content: Occasionally takes ibuprofen for cramps.
facts.source_text: occasional ibuprofen for cramps

facts.content: Takes ORS 3 times a day for 2 days.
facts.source_text: ORS 3x/day x2 days

facts.content: Patient is a graphics designer working from home due to illness.
facts.source_text: Graphics designer; working from home due to illness

facts.content: Patient lives with brother and mother.
facts.source_text: lives with brother and mother

facts.content: Patient is a nonsmoker, consumes an occasional pint, and uses no drugs.
facts.source_text: nonsmoker; occasional pint; no drugs

facts.content: Acute gastroenteritis, likely infectious due to contact and cluster, presenting with 3 days of watery to loose stools, vomiting, and subjective fever.
facts.source_text: Acute gastroenteritis, likely infectious (viral vs bacterial) given contact and cluster; 3 days watery→loose stools, vomiting, subjective fever; no blood; no travel

facts.content: Risk of dehydration exists, but passing urine hourly is a positive sign.
facts.source_text: Risk of dehydration—vomiting but still passing urine hourly (positive sign)

facts.content: Periumbilical abdominal pain is likely secondary to gastroenteritis.
facts.source_text: Periumbilical abdominal pain likely secondary to gastroenteritis

facts.content: Continue ORS with tiny frequent sips to avoid triggering emesis.
facts.source_text: Hydration: Continue ORS; tiny frequent sips to avoid triggering emesis

facts.content: Dietary advice includes simple foods such as toast and biscuits, while avoiding fruit, vegetables, and milk for now.
facts.source_text: Diet: Simple foods (toast/biscuits); avoid fruit, vegetables, and milk for now

facts.content: An urgent clinic appointment is booked for hydration assessment and providing a stool sample for testing.
facts.source_text: Diagnostics: Urgent clinic appt for hydration assessment and to provide stool sample for testing

facts.content: Book urgent appointment via support line.
facts.source_text: Access: Book urgent appointment via support line

facts.content: Seek urgent care or A&E if unable to keep fluids down, have reduced or no urine output, worsening abdominal pain, persistent high fever, blood in stool or urine, confusion, or clinical deterioration.
facts.source_text: Safety net: Seek urgent care/A&E if unable to keep fluids down, reduced/no urine output, worsening abdominal pain, persistent high fever, blood in stool/urine, confusion, or clinical deterioration

facts.content: Call back if there is worsening before the appointment.
facts.source_text: Follow-up: Call back if worsening before appointment
